microtheory.name: robotics
microtheory.definition: Robotics — design, construction, control of robots. Kinematics, dynamics, sensing, planning, manipulation, locomotion, SLAM, human-robot interaction. Foundational figures: Engelberger, Brooks, Khatib, Thrun, Pratt. Industrial + service + humanoid + soft + swarm robotics. Substrate analogue: embodied substrate operating in physical world — the most direct realisation of substrate-as-agent.

concepts.name: robot
concepts.definition: Physical machine sensing + acting autonomously in environment. Karel Čapek's R.U.R. 1920 coined the term.

concepts.name: manipulator
concepts.definition: Robot arm. Links connected by joints. End effector at tip. DOF = degrees of freedom.

concepts.name: mobile_robot
concepts.definition: Locomoting platform. Wheeled, tracked, legged, flying, swimming.

concepts.name: humanoid_robot
concepts.definition: Human-form. ASIMO, Atlas, Optimus. Difficult balance + manipulation. Uncanny valley.

concepts.name: soft_robotics
concepts.definition: Compliant materials. Octopus-inspired. Safer for HRI. Pneumatic actuators.

concepts.name: swarm_robotics
concepts.definition: Many simple robots coordinating. Inspired by ants, bees. Emergent behavior from local rules.

concepts.name: forward_kinematics
concepts.definition: Joint angles → end-effector pose. Forward computation. Denavit-Hartenberg parameters standard.

concepts.name: inverse_kinematics
concepts.definition: Desired end-effector pose → required joint angles. Generally non-unique + non-existent. Critical for motion planning.

concepts.name: jacobian_robotics
concepts.definition: Matrix mapping joint velocities to end-effector velocities. Singularities where rank drops.

concepts.name: denavit_hartenberg
concepts.definition: DH parameters. Standard convention for assigning frames to manipulator links. 4 parameters per link.

concepts.name: workspace
concepts.definition: Set of poses end-effector can reach. Reachable vs dexterous (all orientations).

concepts.name: robot_dynamics
concepts.definition: Forces + torques + motion. Lagrangian or Newton-Euler formulations. M(q)q̈ + C(q,q̇)q̇ + G(q) = τ.

concepts.name: impedance_control
concepts.definition: Hogan. Regulate dynamic relationship between force + motion. Critical for contact tasks. Substrate analogue: substrate's compliant-interaction control.

concepts.name: force_control
concepts.definition: Command force rather than position. Required for assembly, polishing, surgery.

concepts.name: perception_robotics
concepts.definition: Sensing world from sensors. Vision, LIDAR, IMU, force/torque, tactile.

concepts.name: computer_vision_robotics
concepts.definition: Object recognition, pose estimation, depth, segmentation. CNNs revolutionised since 2012.

concepts.name: lidar
concepts.definition: Laser ranging. 3D point clouds. Velodyne. Critical for autonomous driving.

concepts.name: imu
concepts.definition: Inertial Measurement Unit. Accelerometer + gyroscope + (often) magnetometer. State estimation.

concepts.name: tactile_sensing
concepts.definition: Pressure + texture + slip. Critical for manipulation. BioTac, GelSight.

concepts.name: slam
concepts.definition: Simultaneous Localization And Mapping. Robot builds map + tracks own position in it simultaneously. Visual SLAM, LIDAR SLAM. EKF, particle, graph variants.

concepts.name: path_planning
concepts.definition: Find feasible trajectory from start to goal avoiding obstacles. A*, RRT, PRM, optimisation-based.

concepts.name: rrt
concepts.definition: Rapidly-exploring Random Tree. LaValle 1998. Sample-based planning in high-dim spaces. Quickly explores configuration space.

concepts.name: motion_planning
concepts.definition: Beyond path: dynamically-feasible smooth trajectory respecting constraints. Trajectory optimisation.

concepts.name: grasping
concepts.definition: Picking + holding objects. Form closure vs force closure. Generalisation hard — dish-grasping diverse objects.

concepts.name: manipulation_planning
concepts.definition: Sequence of motions + grasps to achieve task. Task and motion planning (TAMP).

concepts.name: deformable_object_manipulation
concepts.definition: Cloth, rope, deformable. Much harder than rigid. Active research.

concepts.name: behavior_based_robotics
concepts.definition: Brooks 1986 subsumption architecture. Layered competences without central planner. Reactive. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflex-driven runtime.

concepts.name: subsumption_architecture
concepts.definition: Brooks. Layers of behavior — higher subsumes lower. No symbolic representation. Insects as inspiration.

concepts.name: hybrid_deliberative_reactive
concepts.definition: Combine deliberate planning (slow, symbolic) with reactive behaviors (fast). Standard modern architecture.

concepts.name: reinforcement_learning_robotics
concepts.definition: Learning control policies through interaction. Sim-to-real challenges. Sample inefficiency.

concepts.name: imitation_learning
concepts.definition: Learn from demonstrations. Behavioral cloning, inverse RL, DAgger.

concepts.name: sim_to_real
concepts.definition: Train in simulation, deploy in real world. Domain randomisation helps. Reality gap perennial challenge.

concepts.name: human_robot_interaction
concepts.definition: HRI. Social robots. Trust, intent recognition, shared autonomy. Substrate analogue: substrate's collaborative-agent interaction.

concepts.name: uncanny_valley
concepts.definition: Mori. Near-human-but-not-quite robots evoke unease. Acceptance dips before rising again.

concepts.name: asimovs_three_laws
concepts.definition: 1. Don't harm humans. 2. Obey unless violates 1. 3. Self-preserve unless violates 1 or 2. Fictional but influential.

rules.name: inverse_kinematics_is_generally_hard
rules.head: Jabberwock plans a manipulation task
rules.body: inverse kinematics has multiple or no solutions in general. Singularities make Jacobian rank-deficient. Numerical or analytical methods per geometry.

rules.name: slam_must_solve_chicken_and_egg
rules.head: Jabberwock navigates an unknown environment
rules.body: localization needs map; mapping needs location. SLAM solves jointly via probabilistic inference. Substrate's joint-state estimation.

rules.name: subsumption_avoids_central_planner_bottleneck
rules.head: Jabberwock designs robot control architecture
rules.body: layered behaviors with higher subsuming lower work without symbolic planner. Brooks 1986. Substrate's reflex-driven design.

rules.name: sim_to_real_gap_demands_domain_randomization
rules.head: Jabberwock trains policies in simulation
rules.body: real-world deployment fails without randomising sim parameters during training. Reality gap principle.

rules.name: contact_tasks_require_impedance_control
rules.head: Jabberwock interacts with environment via contact
rules.body: pure position control fails — small position errors → large forces. Impedance control regulates force-motion relationship. Hogan.
